newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Rate on Yugoslav central bank bonds unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Rate on Yugoslav central bank bonds unchanged.

text.p: The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) left the interest rate on its short-term bonds auctioned on Monday unchanged at a monthly three percent, the Belgrade bourse said.

The three percent monthly rate corresponds to an annual 41.63 percent and is slightly down on an annual 43.28 percent set for the previous tranche of bonds auctioned April 4. The difference results from a different number of days in a month, a central bank source said.
The NBY offered for sale a new 20-million dinar ($3.55 million) tranche of 30-day bonds, issued at a 10,000 dinar face value, but sold only one million dinars worth, the bourse said.
Traders blamed poor liquidity of the banking sector and low interest rate for the low demand.
Last week, the NBY failed to sell any short-term bonds from its tranche due to low offered rate. The size of the tranche and the bonds' rate were identical to the one auctioned today.
($1 = 5.6258 Yugoslav dinars) -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
